anti_overlap: fd-matchmaking-compatibility-weighting covers the mathematical scoring structure; this covers the temporal behavioral sequence of bond formation and maintenance
decision_lens: Bond stability — attraction must convert into pair bond coherence through observable behavioral milestones, or dissipate without them
distance_rationale: Ethologists study the same multi-driver attraction-to-bond progression in real biological systems, but focus on behavioral sequences and timing windows rather than score formulas.
expected_isomorphisms: Attraction-to-bond phase distinction maps to the brainstorm's 'spark vs gradual accumulation' question. Bond maintenance mechanics map to relationship decay systems. Critical period sensitivity maps to elf age/history affecting attraction driver weights.
focus: How pair bonds form in social species — the behavioral sequence, timing windows, and disruption conditions that ethologists study in long-lived pair-bonding animals
name: fd-ethology-pair-bond-formation
persona: Behavioral ecologist who has spent twenty years studying long-term pair bond formation in corvids, prairie voles, and gibbons, with a focus on the conditions that determine whether attraction becomes stable partnership
review_areas: Evaluate whether the design distinguishes attraction (initial draw) from bonding (progressive commitment) — ethology treats these as distinct phases with different drivers and different failure modes

Check whether the 'shared crisis' emotional driver is modeled as a one-time event bonus or as a category of repeated stress-bonding experiences — corvid research shows that repeated mild stressors bond pairs more durably than single extreme events

Assess whether proximity driver correctly models the 'critical period' phenomenon: in most pair-bonding species, early proximity matters more than late proximity — two elves who met young should have stronger proximity bonding potential than two elves who first encounter each other at high age/skill

Evaluate whether the system models bond maintenance vs bond formation differently — an established elf pair should require active maintenance behaviors (co-attendance at revels, continued creative interaction) or the bond decays

Check whether the 'absence makes the heart grow fonder' mechanic is bounded — ethologists find that prolonged separation beyond a threshold breaks bonds entirely rather than strengthening them indefinitely

severity_examples.condition: No phase distinction between attraction accumulation and bond formation event
severity_examples.scenario: Attraction and bonding are the same variable — an elf who reaches high attraction score is treated as bonded with no intermediate behavioral milestone required, producing instant coupling without courtship narrative

severity_examples.condition: Absence modifier has no ceiling and no bond-break threshold at prolonged absence
severity_examples.scenario: Absence mechanic is unbounded: an elf who departs permanently keeps increasing attraction scores in the colony, making absent/departed elves the most romantically potent characters

severity_examples.condition: Shared experience driver is a set (did/didn't happen) rather than a count with diminishing returns
severity_examples.scenario: Shared emotional experiences give a flat bonus regardless of frequency — a couple who survived one crisis is indistinguishable from a couple who survived twelve, losing the accumulated-history depth that makes long relationships feel different from new ones

source_domain: Behavioral ecology and ethology of pair-bonding species
success_hints: The simulation produces recognizable relationship arcs: early attraction that either crystallizes into a bond or fades, established bonds that require maintenance, and occasional late-life pairings that form slowly and feel earned.
task_context: The brainstorm explores 7 categories of romantic attraction drivers for elves; several of them (proximity, shared emotional experience, absence) map directly to ethological pair-bond mechanisms studied in long-lived species.
